title: WhatsApp Medical Report Sharing | AuraPACS
meta: WhatsApp medical report sharing from your PACS: a secure link puts the images and the signed report on the referrer's or patient's phone, with no login.
h1: WhatsApp medical report sharing: images and report on the referrer's phone, no login.
sub: AuraPACS generates a secure link for each study once the report is signed. Front desk sends it on WhatsApp to the referring doctor and the patient. They tap it and see the images and the PDF in a browser. Nobody creates an account, and every view is audited.
meta_ticks: No login for patient or referrer
whatsapp_text: Hi, I'd like to know how AuraPACS shares reports on WhatsApp.
persona: Centre owner whose referrers already ask for reports on WhatsApp and who wants to do it properly

sections.h2: How WhatsApp report sharing works in AuraPACS
paras: When a report is finalised, AuraPACS creates a secure link for that study. The front desk sends the link on WhatsApp to the referring doctor, the patient or both. Opening it shows the images in the browser viewer and the signed PDF, with no app to install and no account to create. Each view is recorded in the audit log.

This replaces the way most Indian centres already share results, which is a phone photo of a printed report or a JPEG of the screen. The link carries the actual study and the actual PDF, comes from the centre's system rather than someone's personal phone, and can be found again later from the patient's history.

sections.h2: Referrers want it on WhatsApp. Centres send it badly.
sections.lead: The channel is not the problem. The problem is what gets sent down it and from whose phone.

items.p: A staff member photographs the printed page and sends it from a personal number. It is blurry, uncropped and unrecoverable a month later.
One slice of a CT, captured from the monitor, stands in for the whole study.

items.h: No record of who received it
items.p: Nobody can say which doctor got which patient's report, or when.
A referrer portal with a username and password is set up and never used. Doctors do not remember passwords for every centre they refer to.

items.h: CDs and film for the images
items.p: The report goes on WhatsApp; the images still travel by courier or patient.
When the staff member leaves, hundreds of reports leave in the chat history.

sections.h2: From sign-off to a tap on a phone.

steps.p: The radiologist finalises the PDF on the study.
AuraPACS creates a secure link for that study.
Front desk sends it to the referrer, the patient, or both.
The recipient sees the images and the report, nothing to install.
The access is logged against the study.
The link and the study remain in the patient's history at the centre.

sections.h2: Practices worth following when sharing on WhatsApp.

items.p: Send to the number the patient or referrer gave at registration, and verify before the first send.
Note at registration that the patient agrees to receive results by WhatsApp and to sharing with the named referrer.

items.b: Share the link, not a file
items.p: The link is served from your system and every view is audited; a forwarded JPEG is not.
Send from the centre's WhatsApp account, not a staff member's personal phone.
Health-record and data-protection rules differ by country and change over time. Confirm your obligations with your advisers.

sections.h2: Getting the result to the referrer, three ways.
rows: Photo of the report, or a disc
Secure link to images and PDF

items.q: Does the referrer need to install anything?
items.a: No. The link opens in the phone's browser and shows the images and the report PDF. There is no app, no account and no password at the recipient's end.
The link is generated per study by AuraPACS and served from the system, and every view of it is audited. Generating links is controlled by role-based access, so only permitted staff can send one.

items.q: Can we see who viewed a report?
items.a: Yes. Views are recorded against the study in the audit log, which is part of the role-based access built into AuraPACS.

items.q: Does the patient get the images or only the PDF?
items.a: The link can open both. Many centres send the report to the patient and the report plus images to the referring doctor; the choice is yours per study.

items.q: Is sharing patient images on WhatsApp allowed?
items.a: Rules on health records and personal data differ by country and are updated over time. Record the patient's consent at registration, send to verified numbers from the centre's own account, and confirm your obligations with your advisers. AuraPACS gives you the audited link; the policy is yours.

items.q: Does this need internet at the centre?
items.a: Yes, for the link to be opened by someone outside. Studies are received and reported on the on-premise node without internet, and links go out once the connection is available. See hybrid PACS.
